title: LEBER OPTIC ATROPHY AND DYSTONIA
alt_titles: LEBER HEREDITARY OPTIC NEUROPATHY WITH DYSTONIA
DYSTONIA, FAMILIAL, WITH VISUAL FAILURE AND STRIATAL LUCENCIES

intro.text: A number sign (#) is used with this entry because of evidence that Leber optic atrophy and dystonia (LDYT) is caused by mutation in mitochondrial DNA, mainly in the MTND6 gene (516006). It has also been reported with mutations in the MTND4 gene (516003).

checks.claim: Leber optic atrophy and dystonia (LDYT) is caused by mutation in mitochondrial DNA.
checks.evidence_quote: LDYT is a unique oxidative phosphorylation disorder caused by mutations in mitochondrial ND6 or ND4 gene.
checks.explanation: The abstract says LDYT is a mitochondrial disorder caused by mtDNA mutations.

checks.claim: Leber optic atrophy and dystonia is caused mainly by mutation in the mitochondrial MTND6 gene.
checks.evidence_quote: The nucleotide G14459A mutation occurs in NADH dehydrogenase subunit 6, and has been suggested previously as the disease-causing mutation in Hispanic, African-American and Caucasian families of Leber's hereditary optic neuropathy (LHON) and/or dystonia.
checks.explanation: ND6 mutation implicated, but the abstract does not say ND6 is the main gene.

checks.claim: Leber optic atrophy and dystonia has also been reported with mutations in the mitochondrial MTND4 gene.
checks.evidence_quote: LDYT is a unique oxidative phosphorylation disorder caused by mutations in mitochondrial ND6 or ND4 gene.
checks.explanation: The abstract names ND4 as a causative gene.

paragraphs.text: Leber optic atrophy and dystonia is a maternally inherited mitochondrial disorder. Within one family, members may have Leber hereditary optic neuropathy (LHON), a childhood-onset neurodegenerative disorder with dystonia and other movement problems, or both. Neuroimaging shows bilateral lesions of the basal ganglia, especially the putamen, like those seen in Leigh syndrome. The disorder is caused by mitochondrial DNA mutations in complex I (NADH dehydrogenase) subunit genes, most often the MTND6 gene.

checks.claim: Leber optic atrophy and dystonia is a maternally inherited mitochondrial disorder.
checks.evidence_quote: A five-generation Hispanic family expressing maternally transmitted Leber hereditary optic neuropathy and/or early-onset dystonia
checks.explanation: The abstract describes maternal transmission and an mtDNA cause.

checks.claim: Within one family affected by Leber optic atrophy and dystonia, members may have Leber hereditary optic neuropathy (LHON), a childhood-onset neurodegenerative disorder with dystonia and other movement problems, or both.
checks.evidence_quote: has been suggested previously as the disease-causing mutation in Hispanic, African-American and Caucasian families of Leber's hereditary optic neuropathy (LHON) and/or dystonia.
checks.explanation: The abstract mentions families with LHON and/or dystonia, and childhood dystonia with late-onset optic neuropathy in this family. It does not explicitly describe variable phenotypes among members of one family.

checks.claim: In Leber optic atrophy and dystonia, neuroimaging shows bilateral lesions of the basal ganglia, especially the putamen, like those seen in Leigh syndrome.
checks.evidence_quote: We investigated a Japanese family with generalized dystonia attributed to striatal degeneration, which occurred in childhood, and late-onset optic neuropathy.
checks.explanation: Striatal degeneration is mentioned; bilateral lesions, putamen and the Leigh-like appearance are not.

checks.claim: Leber optic atrophy and dystonia is caused by mitochondrial DNA mutations in complex I (NADH dehydrogenase) subunit genes.
checks.evidence_quote: Biochemical analysis of a muscle biopsy revealed a severe complex I deficiency, providing a link between these unique mtDNA mutations and this rare, complex phenotype including Leber optic neuropathy.
checks.explanation: The mutations are in the ND4 and ND6 complex I subunit genes, and the paper links them to complex I deficiency.

checks.claim: The mitochondrial gene most often mutated in Leber optic atrophy and dystonia is MTND6.
checks.evidence_quote: The nucleotide G14459A mutation occurs in NADH dehydrogenase subunit 6, and has been suggested previously as the disease-causing mutation in Hispanic, African-American and Caucasian families
checks.explanation: ND6 mutation reported in several families, but 'most often' is not stated.

paragraphs.text: The name Marsden syndrome comes from the report by Marsden et al. (1986) of familial dystonia with visual failure and striatal lucencies.

checks.claim: The name Marsden syndrome comes from the report by Marsden et al. (1986) of familial dystonia with visual failure and striatal lucencies.
checks.evidence_quote: A unique disorder is described in seven members of two families in whom dystonia was variably associated with subacute visual loss
checks.explanation: The paper does report the disorder, but the abstract never mentions the eponym 'Marsden syndrome'.

paragraphs.text: Novotny et al. (1986) described a large Hispanic family in which the disorder passed through the maternal line. Some members had Leber optic atrophy, some had a progressive, generalized dystonia starting in childhood, and some had both. Members with dystonia had lesions of the basal ganglia (striatum) on neuroimaging.

checks.claim: Novotny et al. (1986) described a large Hispanic family in which Leber optic atrophy and dystonia passed through the maternal line.
checks.evidence_quote: We studied a kindred in which 8 members had the neuroretinopathy of Leber's disease; 14 had a progressive, generalized dystonia
checks.explanation: The abstract confirms a large kindred with an inheritance pattern compatible with maternal transmission. It does not say the family was Hispanic.

checks.claim: In the Hispanic family described by Novotny et al. (1986), some members had Leber optic atrophy.
checks.evidence_quote: 8 members had the neuroretinopathy of Leber's disease
checks.explanation: Stated directly in the abstract.

checks.claim: In the Hispanic family described by Novotny et al. (1986), some members had a progressive, generalized dystonia starting in childhood.
checks.evidence_quote: 14 had a progressive, generalized dystonia attributed to striatal degeneration
checks.explanation: The abstract confirms a progressive, generalized dystonia. Childhood onset is not mentioned in the abstract.

checks.claim: In the Hispanic family described by Novotny et al. (1986), some members had both Leber optic atrophy and dystonia.
checks.evidence_quote: and 1 had both disorders.
checks.explanation: Stated directly in the abstract.

checks.claim: In the Hispanic family described by Novotny et al. (1986), members with dystonia had lesions of the basal ganglia (striatum) on neuroimaging.
checks.evidence_quote: a progressive, generalized dystonia attributed to striatal degeneration
checks.explanation: The abstract mentions striatal degeneration but not neuroimaging findings.

paragraphs.text: Marsden et al. (1986) reported familial dystonia with visual failure and lucencies of the striatum on CT scans. This presentation is the origin of the eponym Marsden syndrome.

checks.claim: Marsden et al. (1986) reported familial dystonia with visual failure.
checks.evidence_quote: Familial dystonia and visual failure with striatal CT lucencies.
checks.explanation: The title states this directly.

checks.claim: Marsden et al. (1986) reported lucencies of the striatum on CT scans in familial dystonia with visual failure.
checks.evidence_quote: striking bilateral symmetrical lucencies on CT scan, especially involving the putamen
checks.explanation: The abstract reports striatal (putaminal) lucencies on CT.

checks.claim: The presentation of familial dystonia with visual failure and striatal lucencies reported by Marsden et al. (1986) is the origin of the eponym Marsden syndrome.
checks.evidence_quote: Familial dystonia and visual failure with striatal CT lucencies.
checks.explanation: The paper describes the presentation, but the abstract never mentions the eponym.

paragraphs.text: Bruyn and Went (1964) described a Dutch family with Leber disease and other neurologic abnormalities. This family was later studied at the molecular level by De Vries et al. (1996).

checks.claim: Bruyn and Went (1964) described a Dutch family with Leber disease and other neurologic abnormalities.
checks.explanation: The abstract does not mention Bruyn and Went (1964).

checks.claim: The Dutch family with Leber disease and neurologic abnormalities described by Bruyn and Went (1964) was later studied at the molecular level by De Vries et al. (1996).
checks.evidence_quote: A rare form of Leber hereditary optic neuropathy (LHON) that is associated with hereditary spastic dystonia has been studied in a large Dutch family.
checks.explanation: The paper studied a large Dutch family at the molecular level. The abstract does not say this is the family that Bruyn and Went reported.

paragraphs.text: The pedigrees, including the family of Novotny et al. (1986), showed maternal inheritance, which fits a mitochondrial DNA mutation. Jun et al. (1994) confirmed this by finding a homoplasmic or heteroplasmic mtDNA mutation that passed through the maternal line.

checks.claim: The pedigree of the family reported by Novotny et al. (1986) showed maternal inheritance of Leber optic atrophy and dystonia.
checks.evidence_quote: The mode of inheritance was compatible with maternal transmission.
checks.explanation: Stated directly in the abstract.

checks.claim: Maternal inheritance of Leber optic atrophy and dystonia fits a mitochondrial DNA mutation.
checks.evidence_quote: The mode of inheritance was compatible with maternal transmission. This neurologic disorder may be a mitochondrial disease.
checks.explanation: The abstract reasons from maternal transmission to a likely mitochondrial disease, which matches the claim.

checks.claim: Jun et al. (1994) found a homoplasmic or heteroplasmic mtDNA mutation that passed through the maternal line in Leber optic atrophy and dystonia, confirming mitochondrial inheritance.
checks.evidence_quote: Six maternal relatives in three generations were tested and were found to harbor the mutation, with one female affected with Leber hereditary optic neuropathy being heteroplasmic.
checks.explanation: The mutation was found in maternal relatives, and one of them was heteroplasmic.

paragraphs.text: Jun et al. (1994) studied the Hispanic family first reported by Novotny et al. (1986). In affected members they found a G-to-A transition at nucleotide 14459 in the MTND6 gene, which changes alanine to valine at codon 72 (A72V). The mutation segregated through the maternal line and was linked to both LHON and dystonia.

checks.claim: Jun et al. (1994) studied the Hispanic family with Leber optic atrophy and dystonia first reported by Novotny et al. (1986).
checks.evidence_quote: A five-generation Hispanic family expressing maternally transmitted Leber hereditary optic neuropathy and/or early-onset dystonia
checks.explanation: The Hispanic family is described, but the abstract does not mention Novotny et al. (1986).

checks.claim: Jun et al. (1994) found a G-to-A transition at nucleotide 14459 in the MTND6 gene in affected members of the Hispanic family.
checks.evidence_quote: One of these variants, a G-to-A transition at nucleotide pair (np) 14459, changed a moderately conserved alanine to a valine at NADH dehydrogenase subunit 6 (ND6) residue 72.
checks.explanation: The mutation was identified in an affected child and in maternal relatives.

checks.claim: The MTND6 14459G-A transition changes alanine to valine at codon 72 (A72V).
checks.evidence_quote: changed a moderately conserved alanine to a valine at NADH dehydrogenase subunit 6 (ND6) residue 72
checks.explanation: This is the A72V change.

checks.claim: In the Hispanic family studied by Jun et al. (1994), the MTND6 14459G-A mutation segregated through the maternal line.
checks.evidence_quote: Six maternal relatives in three generations were tested and were found to harbor the mutation
checks.explanation: The mutation segregated through the maternal line.

checks.claim: Jun et al. (1994) linked the MTND6 14459G-A mutation to both LHON and dystonia.
checks.evidence_quote: A mitochondrial DNA mutation at nucleotide pair 14459 of the NADH dehydrogenase subunit 6 gene associated with maternally inherited Leber hereditary optic neuropathy and dystonia.
checks.explanation: The title links the mutation to both LHON and dystonia.

paragraphs.text: Jun et al. (1996) transferred mitochondria carrying the 14459 mutation into transmitochondrial cybrids. The cybrids showed a specific defect in complex I, which tied the biochemical deficiency to the MTND6 mutation.

checks.claim: Jun et al. (1996) transferred mitochondria carrying the MTND6 14459 mutation into transmitochondrial cybrids.
checks.explanation: not supported by any of the 8 cited papers. The abstract does not describe Jun et al. (1996) or cybrid studies.

checks.claim: Cybrids carrying the MTND6 14459 mutation showed a specific complex I defect (Jun et al., 1996).
checks.explanation: not supported by any of the 8 cited papers. No cybrid or complex I data in the abstract.

checks.claim: The cybrid study of Jun et al. (1996) tied the complex I biochemical deficiency to the MTND6 14459 mutation.
checks.explanation: not supported by any of the 8 cited papers. No cybrid or complex I data in the abstract.

paragraphs.text: Shoffner et al. (1995) found the 14459G-A mutation in patients with Leigh syndrome and related neurodegenerative disease. This widened the range of phenotypes linked to this mutation.

checks.claim: Shoffner et al. (1995) found the MTND6 14459G-A mutation in patients with Leigh syndrome and related neurodegenerative disease.
checks.explanation: not supported by any of the 8 cited papers. The abstract does not mention Shoffner et al. or Leigh syndrome.

checks.claim: The finding of Shoffner et al. (1995) widened the range of phenotypes linked to the MTND6 14459G-A mutation.
checks.explanation: not supported by any of the 8 cited papers. Not addressed in the abstract.

paragraphs.text: De Vries et al. (1996) studied the Dutch family with LHON and neurologic abnormalities first reported by Bruyn and Went (1964). They found the 11696 mutation in the MTND4 gene together with a mutation at nucleotide 14596 in the MTND6 gene.

checks.claim: De Vries et al. (1996) studied the Dutch family with LHON and neurologic abnormalities first reported by Bruyn and Went (1964).
checks.evidence_quote: A rare form of Leber hereditary optic neuropathy (LHON) that is associated with hereditary spastic dystonia has been studied in a large Dutch family.
checks.explanation: The paper studied a Dutch family with LHON and dystonia. The abstract does not identify it as the family that Bruyn and Went (1964) first reported.

checks.claim: De Vries et al. (1996) found the 11696 mutation in the MTND4 gene in the Dutch family with LHON and neurologic abnormalities.
checks.evidence_quote: A heteroplasmic A-->G transition at nucleotide position 11696 in the ND4 gene resulted in the substitution of an isoleucine for valine at amino acid position 312.
checks.explanation: The 11696 ND4 mutation was found in the family.

checks.claim: De Vries et al. (1996) found a mutation at nucleotide 14596 in the MTND6 gene together with the MTND4 11696 mutation in the Dutch family.
checks.evidence_quote: A second mutation, a homoplasmic T-->A transition at nucleotide position 14596 in the ND6 gene, resulted in the substitution of a methionine for the isoleucine at amino acid residue 26.
checks.explanation: The 14596 ND6 mutation was found together with the 11696 mutation.

paragraphs.text: The cybrid studies of Jun et al. (1996) indicated that the 14459 MTND6 mutation lowers complex I activity of the mitochondrial respiratory chain. Damage to the striatum and optic nerve is thought to result from this energy defect.

checks.claim: The cybrid studies of Jun et al. (1996) indicated that the MTND6 14459 mutation lowers complex I activity of the mitochondrial respiratory chain.
checks.explanation: not supported by any of the 8 cited papers. The abstract does not mention cybrid studies or complex I activity.

checks.claim: Damage to the striatum and optic nerve in Leber optic atrophy and dystonia is thought to result from the complex I energy defect.
checks.explanation: not supported by any of the 5 cited papers. The abstract does not discuss an energy-defect mechanism.
